tutorial.title: Using Variables
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to update and reuse variables.

lessons.title: Updating a variable
lessons.interactiveContent:
We already saw that let variables, as opposed to const can change and update the values they store.

Use the = sign to change the value in status from "Watching Netflix" to "Relaxing at the beach".

Make sure to pick =.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We already saw that let variables, as opposed to const can change and update the values they store.

Change currentStatus from "Watching Netflix" so the console displays "Relaxing at the beach".

Make sure to pick currentStatus, followed by =.

lessons.title: As often as we want
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can update let variables as often as we want.

Try it yourself: change the value of currentStatus to "Reading".

Make sure to pick currentStatus, followed by =, and finally "Reading".
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can update let variables as often as we want.

After the first status is displayed, update the existing variable so the next console line reads "Reading".

Make sure to pick currentStatus, followed by =, and finally "Reading".

lessons.title: Setting with other variables
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also give variables the values of other variables by setting one variable to the other.

Give the currentStatus variable the value of defaultStatus.

Make sure to pick defaultStatus.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can also give variables the values of other variables by setting one variable to the other.

Use the other variable in the assignment so currentStatus displays "Hi there!".

Make sure to pick defaultStatus.

lessons.title: Last value
lessons.interactiveContent:
When we update a variable, it forgets its previous value.

Display the currentStatus variable when it's set to "Playing football" and when it's set to "Walking the dog".

Make sure to pick currentStatus, followed by currentStatus.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When we update a variable, it forgets its previous value.

Pass the variable currentStatus to both calls to display its value before and after the update.

Make sure to pick currentStatus, followed by currentStatus.

lessons.title: The missing let keyword
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of these lines of code updates the currentStatus variable?

currentStatus = "Working out";let currentStatus = "Working out";

currentStatus = "Working out";.
lessons.hardModeContent:
currentStatus already exists. Which line changes its stored value without declaring it again?

currentStatus = "Working out";let currentStatus = "Working out";const currentStatus = "Working out";

currentStatus = "Working out";.

lessons.title: Displaying a status
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

Watching NetflixcurrentStatus

Watching Netflix.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which change makes the console display currentStatus as text instead of its stored value?

Put quotes around currentStatus inside console.log()Put quotes around the variable name in its declarationReplace const with let

Put quotes around currentStatus inside console.log().

lessons.title: Finding the bug
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with this code?

It misses the let keyword in the first lineNothing

It misses the let keyword in the first line.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The second line updates firstName. What must the first line do before that update is valid?

It misses the let keyword in the first lineNothingIt needs const in the second line

It misses the let keyword in the first line.

lessons.title: Displaying a name
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

JoeLori

Make sure to pick Joe.
lessons.hardModeContent:
firstName is assigned twice before it is logged. Which value remains when the console line runs?

JoeLoriBoth values

Make sure to pick Joe.

lessons.title: Updating the temperature
lessons.interactiveContent:
Change the value in the temperature variable to "100 degrees".

Make sure to pick temperature.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Change the value in the temperature variable so the console displays "100 degrees".

Make sure to pick temperature.

lessons.title: Updating a status
lessons.interactiveContent:
Update the currentStatus variable to "Writing code".

Make sure to pick currentStatus followed by = and then "Writing code", ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Update the existing currentStatus variable so the console displays "Writing code".

Make sure to pick currentStatus, followed by =, "Writing code", and finally ;.

lessons.title: Updating button text
lessons.interactiveContent:
Update the buttonText variable to "Log in".

Make sure to pick buttonText followed by = and then "Log in", ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Update the existing buttonText variable so the console displays "Log in".

Make sure to pick buttonText, followed by =, "Log in", and finally ;.

lessons.title: Finishing up
lessons.interactiveContent:
Change the value of the currentStatus variable to "Done".

Make sure to type "Done".

lessons.title: Adding string values
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can add string values together with a + sign.

Add the values "Followers:" and "55" together.

Make sure to pick +.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can add string values together with a + sign.

Join "Followers:" and "55" into one string expression.

Make sure to pick +.

lessons.title: Displaying expressions
lessons.interactiveContent:
We call adding together string values an expression because it creates a single string value.

Add the expression between the parentheses of console.log().

Make sure to pick "Followers:", followed by +, and finally "55".
lessons.hardModeContent:
We call adding together string values an expression because it creates a single string value.

Place the expression in console.log() so it displays Followers:55.

Make sure to pick "Followers:", followed by +, and finally "55".

lessons.title: Expressions with variables
lessons.interactiveContent:
When expressions contain variables, they use the values in the variables.

Create an expression that adds the value "Followers:" and the variable followers together.

Make sure to pick "Followers:", followed by +, and finally followers.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You join strings with +. This expression creates one string. A variable in an expression supplies its stored value.

Join "Followers:" first and the variable followers second.

Make sure to pick "Followers:", followed by +, and finally followers.

lessons.title: Display expression
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use console.log() to see the results of expressions.

Add a console.log() instruction around the expression.

Make sure to pick console.log, followed by (, and finally ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can use console.log() to see the results of expressions.

Wrap the expression in the display call so the console shows Followers:55.

Make sure to pick console.log, followed by (, and finally ).

lessons.title: Setting the result of an expression
lessons.interactiveContent:
Since expressions become values, we can give them to variables just like values.

Store the expression "Posts:" + "13" in the variable label and display it in the console.

Make sure to pick "Posts:" followed by + and then "13", label.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Since expressions become values, we can give them to variables just like values.

Join two strings in label, then display the variable so the console shows Posts:13.

Make sure to pick "Posts:", followed by +, "13", and finally label.

lessons.title: The value of label
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the value of label?

"Name:Joe""Joe"

Make sure to pick "Name:Joe".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Evaluate both strings in the expression. What exact string is stored in label?

"Name:Joe""Joe""Name: Joe"

Make sure to pick "Name:Joe".

lessons.title: Displaying nothing
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

Nothing, because there's no console.log() instructionJonathan

Nothing, because there's no console.log() instruction.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which change makes this code display Jonathan on one line in the console?

Put the whole expression inside console.log()Store the expression in a variable without logging itUse a separate console.log() for each string

Put the whole expression inside console.log().

lessons.title: Updating a variable
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

Username:snoopdoggsnoopdogg

Make sure to pick Username:snoopdogg.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The expression includes a label and the value stored in username. What exact text does the console receive?

Username:snoopdoggsnoopdoggUsername: username

Make sure to pick Username:snoopdogg.

lessons.title: Missing whitespace
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why does this code display SteveJobs without a space in the console?

Because "Steve" + "Jobs" adds the values together without a spaceBecause console.log() never displays spaces

Because "Steve" + "Jobs" adds the values together without a space.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The output has no gap between the names. Which part of the expression determines that?

Because "Steve" + "Jobs" adds the values together without a spaceBecause console.log() never displays spacesBecause + automatically removes spaces

Because "Steve" + "Jobs" adds the values together without a space.

lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the temperature variable to the expression.

lessons.hardModeContent:
Add the temperature variable to the expression so it displays 14 degrees.

Make sure to pick temperature.

lessons.title: Displaying number of posts
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display Posts:55 in the console.

Make sure to pick console.log followed by ( and then "Posts:" + "55", ), ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Display Posts:55 by joining "Posts:" and "55" in a console call.

Make sure to pick console.log, followed by (, "Posts:" + "55", ), and finally ;.

lessons.title: Displaying a name
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display Ms. Irene in the console.

Make sure to pick title, followed by +, and finally name.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use the two variables to make the console display Ms. Irene with its included space.

Make sure to pick title, followed by +, and finally name.

lessons.title: Displaying number of likes
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the string value "likes" to see how many likes we have.

Make sure to type "likes".

lessons.title: Numbers have no quotes
lessons.interactiveContent:
There are other kinds of values, too. Like numbers, which have no double quotes around them.

Make sure to pick 5.
lessons.hardModeContent:
There are other kinds of values, too. Like numbers, which have no double quotes around them. Set the constant to the number five.

Make sure to pick 5.

lessons.title: Setting numbers
lessons.interactiveContent:
Numbers make it easier to keep track of numeric values. For example, the number of likes on a Facebook post.

Create a numberOfLikes variable and set it to 5.

Make sure to pick const followed by numberOfLikes and then =, 5.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Numbers make it easier to keep track of numeric values. For example, the number of likes on a Facebook post.

Declare numberOfLikes with the number that makes the console display 5.

Make sure to pick const, followed by numberOfLikes, =, and finally 5.

lessons.title: Addition and subtraction
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can create expressions with numbers, too. We add numbers together with the + sign and subtract them from each other with the - sign.

Display 6 in the console by setting numberOfLikes to 5 + 1.

Make sure to pick +, followed by 1.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can create expressions with numbers, too. We add numbers together with the + sign and subtract them from each other with the - sign.

Make numberOfLikes display 6 using 5 and one more number.

Make sure to pick +, followed by 1.

lessons.title: Multiplication and division
lessons.interactiveContent:
We use the * sign to multiply numbers and the / sign to divide numbers.

Turn 0.5 into its percent value by multiplying it by 100.

Make sure to pick *.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We use the * sign to multiply numbers and the / sign to divide numbers.

Turn 0.5 into 50 before it is displayed.

Make sure to pick *.

lessons.title: Calculating with variables
lessons.interactiveContent:
When we store numbers in variables, we can use the variables for calculations, too.

Add 1 to the numberOfSteps variable before displaying it in the console.

Make sure to pick +, followed by 1.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When we store numbers in variables, we can use the variables for calculations, too.

Make the second console line show the next step after 70.

Make sure to pick +, followed by 1.

lessons.title: Calculate the total 3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Since expressions become values, we can store calculation results in variables.

Store the calculation result in the total variable.

Make sure to pick total, followed by =, and finally private + public.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Since expressions become values, we can store calculation results in variables.

The shown names private and public cannot be identifiers in strict mode; here, focus on the combined expression.

Create the variable that stores the combined post count before it is added to the label.

Make sure to pick total, followed by =, and finally private + public.

What's the value of the speed variable?

305300

Make sure to pick 305.
lessons.hardModeContent:

3053003005

lessons.title: Displaying the temperature
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why does this code display 31 instead of 4 in the console?

Because "3" and "1" are string valuesBecause the expression subtracts the numbers

Because "3" and "1" are string values.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The expression uses +, but it logs 31. Which detail in the code explains that result?

Both operands are strings because they are in double quotes.The variable name temperature changes the addition rule.console.log() converts the result to text.

Both operands are strings because they are in double quotes.

lessons.title: Identifying a number
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we know that the score variable stores a number?

Because there are no double quotes around 40 and 4Because score sounds like it stores a number

Because there are no double quotes around 40 and 4.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Before running the line, which code detail tells you that score will store a number?

The values 40 and 4 have no double quotes.The name score is commonly used for numbers.The keyword const makes every value a number.

The values 40 and 4 have no double quotes.

lessons.title: Displaying the area
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

3 * 515

lessons.hardModeContent:

The text 3 * 5.The number 15.An instruction that multiplies 3 by 5.

The text 3 * 5.

lessons.interactiveContent:
Multiply the savings variable by the interest variable.

Make sure to pick *, followed by interest.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You multiply numbers with *.

Use both variables, with savings first, to calculate and display the interest amount 4.

Make sure to pick savings, followed by *, and finally interest.

lessons.title: Calculating the average
lessons.interactiveContent:
Divide sumOfGrades by numberOfStudents to get the average grade of a class.

Make sure to pick /.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You divide numbers with /. To get an average grade, divide the total grades by the number of students.

Use the variables to make the class average display 92.

Make sure to pick sumOfGrades, followed by /.

Make sure to pick total, followed by -, and finally discount.
lessons.hardModeContent:

Make sure to pick total, followed by -, and finally discount.
